criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core (run: cargo test -p athena-core) lands a job on a branch with a bare-repo remote copy, resyncs onto a squash-merged main, and asserts the branch is a descendant of both its previous remote head and the merged commit (git is_ancestor both ways true), and that a plain push (push_branch) then succeeds.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 1 passed. The test (land.rs) pushes `work` to a bare origin made with `git init --bare`, calls resync_tip and then reset_keep, and asserts is_ancestor(previous_remote_head, tip) and is_ancestor(squash, tip). It then runs push_branch("origin","work",&tip), which succeeds, and checks that the bare repo's branch equals tip. As a contrast, git.replay(...) gives a commit that is not a descendant of the old remote head, and push_branch of it errors. Athena's fails-without run of this command exited 101, but only because the test did not compile without the fix.

criteria.criterion: A drain test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (run: cargo test -p athena-cli drain) shows the working branch is pushed after each landing, once per landed job, with a plain push; a failed push is shown as a warning and the landing stays landed.
criteria.evidence: All passed. In drain.rs, the_drain_pushes_the_working_branch_after_each_landing asserts that the number of pushes equals the number of landings, that a `push` call comes straight after each `land`, and that a Rejected outcome makes no push. tests/drain.rs drives RealSteps against a real bare origin. the_real_steps_push... shows origin's `work` moving from the earlier head to the head at landing, with one `pushed work to origin` line. a_refused_push_is_a_warning... shows a divergent origin left unchanged (so the push is not forced), a `warning: could not push work to origin` line, and report.landed == 1 with landing text `landed`. a_lander_that_pushes_itself... shows no second push. Gap: each test lands only one job (the Stub queues one item), so more than one landing is never shown. The hook does sit inside the per-landing path of Drain::land.

criteria.criterion: resync_tip/resync_onto_merge in crates/athena-core/src/land.rs no longer call git.replay or otherwise rewrite existing branch commits; the diff shows a merge commit instead, and no force or push_if_remote_at is used for the working branch push (Grep for --force in the diff finds none).
criteria.evidence: In the diff, resync_tip now calls git.merge_tree(landed, head, merged) and git.commit_tree(&tree, &[head, merged], ...). The only `replay(` left in land.rs is in the test's contrast (line 747). push_working_branch uses GitRemote::push, which runs `git push origin <commit>:refs/heads/<branch>` (remote.rs:52) with no force and no push_if_remote_at. The -G search finds only land.rs (the removed replay call and the test's replay contrast) and the CHANGELOG prose; no `--force` was added. resync_tip_adds_a_merge_commit_and_rewrites_nothing passed: parents are [head, squash], every old commit is an ancestor, and the tree equals head's.

criteria.criterion: A test shows the unchanged no-op cases (merged already an ancestor of head; landed not on head) and a conflicting merge leaves the branch unchanged with an error (cargo test -p athena-core).
criteria.evidence: All passed. resync_tip_leaves_the_no_op_cases_alone gets None for a second run, for an older base commit as `merged`, and for two heads that do not hold `landed`. a_squash_the_later_work_conflicts_with_is_an_error_that_moves_nothing errors with `conflicts` and head is unchanged. a_squash_with_governed_content_the_branch_lacks... names other.txt and head is unchanged. resync_onto_merge_reports_a_conflict_and_leaves_the_branch_unchanged asserts the error says `the branch is unchanged` and athena.head() is the same. a_hand_made_merge_that_takes_older_governed_content_is_not_records_only is refused by classify_commit.

criteria.criterion: athena land --pr pushes the working branch after the landing; a test covers it in crates/athena-core/src/gh/tests.rs or the CLI tests.
criteria.evidence: 6 passed. The tests are in gh/after_merge_tests.rs, a test module of gh declared in gh/mod.rs:111. They go through Athena::after_merge, which land_pr calls at landing.rs:954 for both `athena land --pr` and PrLander. after_a_merge_the_working_branch_is_pushed_and_a_report_that_did_not_land_pushes_nothing shows the bare origin's `work` moving to a commit that descends from base, landed and the squash, with the `pushed work to origin` line after the merge line. A report that did not land pushes nothing. A missing origin gives a warning and Ok. A `main` checkout is not pushed. The real `gh` command itself is not run (it needs the network).

criteria.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for f9d1b7a4 (CI run 42557910068): fmt passed, clippy passed, test passed. I did not rerun them.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the append-only resync and the push after each landing.
criteria.evidence: Under Unreleased there are three bullets: the append-only resync with the merge commit; the plain push after each landing, which never forces, never pushes the default branch, and treats a refusal as a warning; and landing records leaving out commits already landed, with the growing PR range and D167. A Fixed bullet names the root cause (the replay gave the commits new ids) and the 2026-10-27 symptom. The known limit before the cutover is pinned in a gate test, but the CHANGELOG itself does not mention it.

criteria.criterion: Docs and doc comments that describe the branch being rebuilt/rewritten (resync_onto_merge doc, after_merge comment) are updated to describe the merge commit.
criteria.evidence: The resync_tip and resync_onto_merge docs, the after_merge doc and inline comment, the close_carried_prs comment, the pr_commits_excluding doc and the test_support.rs comments now describe the merge and the push. The ui line now says `merged the host's commit`. A search of these files finds `replay` only for other features (stack rebase, candidate replay). Docs outside scope are still stale (see findings).

findings.summary: The new filter in records.rs, which leaves out commits that earlier landings already hold, has no test that fails without it. The planned tests for a second landing after a resync were dropped.
findings.evidence: GitLandingRecords::commits now reads every landing record and leaves out head_sha when host_commit is an ancestor of the base. Only pr_commits_excluding is unit-tested (land.rs commits_of_a_landed_head_are_left_out_of_a_pull_request_range). A Grep finds no tests named landing_records_leave_out_landed_commits, realistic_branch or open_earlier_pull_request, although the planned demonstration for criterion 5 named them, so those test-name filters would match no test. No test runs a second land_pr on a branch that already holds a resync merge, which is the drain case. From reading pr_check::check_pr_head and gate classify_pre_merge, I expect that path to pass, but this is not shown.

findings.summary: The drain tests show one landing and one push, never two landings each followed by a push.
findings.evidence: The Stub queue returns one item (drain.rs:4728), and the RealSteps tests assert report.landed == 1. The plan called for two landings, with origin checked at the second ask. The per-landing behaviour follows from the hook being placed in Drain::land, but no test shows it.

findings.summary: On a `main` checkout the resync now makes a merge commit on local `main` instead of moving `main` onto the squash commit. The fixtures were changed to avoid this, and the CHANGELOG does not mention it.
findings.evidence: Both fixtures now use reset_keep, because a merge commit on main would put C0 off main's first-parent line. split_from_main treats refs/heads/main as main, so a local `athena check --history` on such a checkout would judge the landed commit and the merge by attribution. A simpler fix: when the branch is the default branch, or nothing on it follows `landed`, fast-forward to `merged`.

findings.summary: Some design docs still say Athena rebuilds the branch after a squash and does not push. docs/architecture.md is not named as a follow-up.
findings.evidence: architecture.md: 'rebuilds the local branch after a squash (D88)'. enforcement.md: 'Athena does not push in v0'. The CHANGELOG names enforcement.md, native-pr-landing.md 5.2a and D88 as follow-ups, but not architecture.md. These files are outside the deliverables list, so leaving them unedited is right.

findings.summary: Scope: records.rs is a production file outside the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: The deliverables list does not include records.rs (the planned files did). The change follows from keeping landed commits on the branch, and the CHANGELOG explains it. Test-only files outside the list (tests/drain.rs, gh/after_merge_tests.rs, athena-gate landing_tests.rs) only add tests.

findings.summary: A landing confirmed through an existing merge (no local landed commit) is not pushed. push_working_branch always uses `origin`, even if land --pr was given another remote.
findings.evidence: after_merge pushes only inside `if let (Some(landed), Some(merged))`. PrLander.pushes_working_branch() is true, so the drain does not push in that case either. push_working_branch hard-codes the name "origin".

findings.summary: Before the cutover, the history check refuses a head that holds both a landed job and its squash. This is pinned in a gate test.
findings.evidence: The new test pins that the old full walk reports 'already landed' for the merge shape. The repo's athena.toml sets cutover_job 20261025-001232-vesh, and the evidence snapshot's landings/20261025-011748-0kfe.json mentions vesh, which suggests (I did not verify) that the real repo is past the cutover and unaffected.

summary: The change does what was asked. After a landing, `resync_tip` no longer rewrites the branch with `git.replay`. It adds one merge commit whose parents are the old tip and the commit the host made, so the branch stays a descendant of its remote copy. A new `Athena::push_working_branch` pushes the branch with a plain push: never forced, never to the default branch, and a refused push is only a warning, so the landing stands. `athena land --pr` reaches it through `after_merge`. `athena drain` reaches it through a new `Steps::push_after_landing` hook, which skips landers that already push, so each landing is pushed once. I ran the planned tests one at a time and all passed: the bare-remote ancestry and plain-push test (the old replay result is shown being refused), the merge-shape test, the no-op and conflict tests, the after_merge push tests, the drain stub test, and three RealSteps drain tests against a bare origin. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's CI record. CHANGELOG.md has entries, and the doc comments describe the merge. Nothing blocks the change, but there are five minor findings. (1) Later landings now leave out commits that an earlier landing record already holds (new code in records.rs). Only the low-level helper is tested, and the planned tests for a second landing after a resync were dropped; their test-name filters match no test, so those commands pass without running anything. (2) The drain tests land only one job each, not two. (3) On a `main` checkout the resync now makes a merge commit on local `main`; the test fixtures were switched to `reset --keep` to avoid this. (4) docs/architecture.md and docs/enforcement.md still describe the old behaviour. (5) records.rs was changed although it is not on the deliverables list.
